interview.name: Morning sheet report
interview.looks: one sheet tab the owner picks, with any columns, and what it remembered yesterday: the row count and the total of each number column
interview.handles: work out what changed since yesterday: how many rows there are now and how many were added, and for each number column today's total and its change from yesterday; write it as a short plain message of a few lines
interview.finish: the owner got one short summary on Telegram, and today's row count and totals are remembered for tomorrow
interview.asks: nothing: it only reads the sheet and messages the owner, and never changes the sheet
interview.remembers: yesterday's row count and column totals, as a record { rows, totals }

job.does: Each morning it compares your sheet tab with yesterday's (how many rows, and the total of each number column) and sends you a short summary on Telegram.
job.done: You get a Telegram message with what changed since yesterday, and today's numbers are kept for tomorrow.

settings.label: Which Google Sheet tab should I summarize?
settings.help: Pick the tab with your daily data

memory.description: Previous day's row count and totals for each number column, as {rows: number, totals: {column_name: number, ...}}

steps.title: Read sheet and compare to yesterday
steps.description: Read the sheet tab provided in settings. Count rows and sum each numeric column into column_totals. Read yesterday's values from memory key yesterday, a record shaped {rows: number, totals: {column_name: number}} (the shape the save step writes): yesterday's row count is yesterday.rows and its totals are yesterday.totals. Calculate new_rows added and column_changes for each column total against them. Compose summary_text as a short plain message of a few lines listing row count change and each column's total change. If there is no yesterday in memory, say this is the first run.

steps.title: Save today's state for tomorrow
steps.description: Store today's row count and column totals in memory under key 'yesterday' for tomorrow's comparison. Save as {rows: row_count, totals: {column_name: total_value, ...}}.

read_sheet.note: The code correctly reads the sheet, calculates row counts and column totals, retrieves yesterday's data from memory, computes changes, and returns all required outputs in the specified format without calling any tools beyond those listed or performing unsafe operations.

save_state.note: The code performs the stated step by storing today's row count and column totals under the 'yesterday' key, reads only its inputs, returns an empty object as specified, calls only the listed memory tool, and avoids unsafe behavior.
